reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 is a computational design study for single-phase solid solutions, not precipitation. E2 shows high corrosion resistance in Mg-Ti-Zn alloys due to a Ti-rich surface film, not Mg-rich intermetallic precipitation. E3 mentions diffusion-driven precipitation of Al2Cu and Mg2Si in Al-based alloys, but these are not Mg-rich lightweight HEAs and the link to improved corrosion/oxidation via reduced galvanic activity is not established.
premises: Annealing drives diffusion-controlled precipitation of Mg-rich intermetallics from a supersaturated solid solution in Mg-containing lightweight HEAs
Sluggish diffusion in multi-principal element alloys governs the precipitation kinetics
Precipitation reduces micro-galvanic differences by adjusting local elemental distributions
A more uniform, less galvanically active microstructure improves corrosion resistance
The transformed microstructure promotes an adherent, protective oxide layer during high-temperature oxidation
